Maladaptive Strategies.value: I keep myself constantly surrounded by people so I am never alone with my thoughts
give up important responsibilities to stay safe or avoid triggers
constantly scan environment for signs of threat

Threat.value: My body reacts to danger before I have even had time to think
Unusual silence makes me feel something dangerous is about to happen

Negative Appraisals.value: I should have protected others and I failed
I am permanently an outsider now

vignette: Amina is a 68-year-old Middle Eastern woman who has been working as a prison guard for over two decades. She married her husband, Khalid, 45 years ago and they have always supported each other through the challenges of life. On a seemingly ordinary day at work, Amina's world was turned upside down when she witnessed a violent assault on another inmate by a group of fellow prisoners. Despite her efforts to intervene, she felt powerless as she watched the attack unfold, unable to prevent it from escalating. Since that traumatic event, Amina has been struggling with intense fear and anxiety. She constantly scans her environment for signs of potential danger, never feeling truly safe in any setting. At home, she often finds herself checking every corner and shadow, convinced that something terrible could happen if she lets her guard down. The unusual silence around the house only heightens her sense of vulnerability; it feels as though the quiet is a precursor to an impending threat. Amina has developed a relentless need for social engagement, finding solace in constant company. She rarely spends time alone, even when at home with Khalid. Her reasoning is simple: if she is surrounded by people, then the danger cannot come for her unnoticed. This behavior has strained her relationship; Khalid often feels neglected as Amina's focus on safety overshadows their shared moments. Her responsibilities have also taken a hit. At work, Amina finds it increasingly difficult to carry out her duties with full engagement. She has started to drop important tasks that she perceives as too risky or stressful, leading to a decline in her job performance and feedback from supervisors about the need for improvement. The trauma has left deep emotional scars. Amina feels an overwhelming sense of guilt, believing that if she had been more vigilant or stronger, she could have prevented the assault. This belief has transformed into a pervasive feeling that she is now an outsider, disconnected from both her colleagues and community. Trust in others has eroded; she no longer believes that anyone can truly be relied upon. Amina's sleep problems are another major challenge. She finds it nearly impossible to fall asleep at night because her body reacts before her mind can process any perceived threats. Even the slightest noise or change in silence sends her into a state of high alert, making restful sleep an elusive goal. The cumulative effects of these symptoms have gradually taken their toll on Amina's daily life and relationships. Khalid has become increasingly concerned about his wife's well-being and has encouraged her to seek help. It was the realization that her constant need for socializing and avoidance behaviors were affecting both her work and home life that finally pushed Amina to take action. When she came in for therapy, Amina expressed a deep fear of losing control again and being unable to protect herself or others from harm. At the same time, she is hopeful that with support, she can regain a sense of security and reconnect with those around her. She hopes to find ways to manage her anxiety without sacrificing her relationships and responsibilities. Through this journey, Amina aims to rebuild trust in both herself and others while learning coping strategies that will allow her to feel safe and secure once more.
